title: Model beside the text
statement: Model a reading only after students have read the whole text, and do it beside the text rather than after it.
detail: Rulings on lesson structure (2026-07-16) say the child reads the whole passage before anything is modelled, and the modelling happens beside the passage, showing how to locate, re-read and reject candidate evidence on the actual text; a later ruling (2026-07-24) says it models the thinking, why this detail and not that one and what was rejected, never just a filled-in organiser (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0180-lesson-structure-procedure-rulings.qmd`). A review of showcase lessons found a model that treated picking the right animal as easy when the text also mentions two others, and asked that it show the choice is genuinely difficult (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0136-g3-reading-v2-reviewer-feedback.qmd`). The modelling should also never make the thinking look easier than it is.
against: Rereading is a different matter: a later review said not to make whole-text repetition a universal ritual, and to reread the parts that serve the lesson's knowledge objective (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0172-g3-reading-course-feedback-2026-08-04.qmd`).

evidence.quote: the child reads the *whole* passage before anything is modelled, and the modelling moment happens *beside* the passage
the I-do must model *thinking* — why this detail and not that one, what was rejected and why — never just reveal a filled-in organiser.
The model should show that selecting the relevant animal and adaptation is genuinely difficult.
As built, the quote has been lifted out of the script, which means the app has already done the locating for the child.
Marking it in place shows where the evidence came from — and locating evidence in the text is the SEARCH and FIND skill.
Do not lift the quote out of the script. Extracting it performs the locating step for the child.
Keep the script on the left in guided practice. Mark the key quote in place within it.
The student reads the complete passage (with a **read-aloud option** available — "hear it") *before any modeling*.
The five source-reading sections precede interpretation.
D1.9 Read before model — the full 4-part story (p6/p8/p10/p12) is read in its entirety before the I-do (p19); order confirmed by page sequence.
